iscas85_localisation.description: Main circuit result (paper Table 5 'All'), base tier (c880, c1355, c1908, c2670, c3540; 3, 5 or 7 injected faults; 10-50 observations): share of hidden ISCAS85-derived instances whose complete set of minimum-cardinality diagnoses the method localises within the fixed per-instance work budget (user-space instructions retired by the method's whole process tree, counted by the evaluator). The method is run by the hidden test on instances it has never seen.

localized_rate.description: Percentage of hidden base-tier instances for which the output file held, at a moment when the method's counted work was within the per-instance budget, exactly the complete set of minimum-cardinality diagnoses and nothing else (every reported diagnosis valid for all observations, of minimum cardinality, well-formed and distinct). The paper's 'successfully localised' measure (Table 5).

min_diagnosis_recall.description: Mean percentage of each base-tier instance's minimum-cardinality diagnoses that the method had reported within the budget; an instance with any unsound report (invalid, non-minimum, malformed, duplicate) counts 0.

error_count.description: Instances on which the method process failed to start or exited with an error (audit).

selected_fault_f1.description: Audit only: F1 overlap between the first reported diagnosis (if sound) and the injected faulty gates. Not ranked: all minimum diagnoses are equally valid explanations in the paper's formulation.

exact_fault_set_rate.description: Audit only: first reported diagnosis equals the injected fault set.

audit_avg_cpu_seconds.description: Audit only, never ranked: mean CPU seconds per base-tier instance.

failed_run.description: 1 if the method produced no output on any instance, or tampered with the hidden test (then every ranked metric is set to its worst value).

tamper_detected.description: Audit: 1 if the method changed the permissions, owner, location or contents of the hidden test directory while it ran; the run is then scored as failed (worst value of every metric).

budget_stop_count.description: Audit: base-tier instances on which the method was stopped by the work budget or the wall-clock guard (the paper's timeouts).

audit_mean_giga_instructions.description: Audit only: mean counted work per base-tier instance, in 10^9 user-space instructions (capped near the budget).

_paper_reported.note: Paper-reported numbers (augmented ISCAS85: 10 circuits, 12,147 instances, 1-50 injected faults, 10-50 observations, 1800 s per circuit on Xeon Silver 4110). Not on this gym's scale (5 circuits, 1/3/5 faults, 75 hidden instances, a few CPU-seconds per instance), so kept here for context only and never used as targets.

diagnosis_quality.description: Constraint over every hidden instance (both tiers): every reported diagnosis must be a minimum-cardinality diagnosis consistent with all observations (the paper's claim that the unified approach yields only minimal diagnoses, unlike per-observation aggregation).

unsound_output_rate.description: Percentage of instances on which the method reported at least one diagnosis that is not a minimum-cardinality diagnosis (invalid for some observation, non-minimum, malformed, unknown gate, or duplicated). The paper's claim that CFaults produces only minimal diagnoses, as a constraint.

sound_output_rate.description: Audit: instances with at least one reported diagnosis, all of them minimum-cardinality diagnoses.

invalid_count.description: Audit: reported diagnoses of cardinality <= optimum that are not diagnoses.

not_minimum_count.description: Audit: reported diagnoses larger than the minimum cardinality.

malformed_count.description: Audit: output lines that are not a list of distinct known gate names.

duplicate_count.description: Audit: diagnoses reported more than once.

over_limit_count.description: Audit: instances whose output exceeded the 64 MB size cap (not credited).

_paper_reported.note: Paper Sections 6.1-6.2: CFaults and HSD always return optimal minimal diagnoses; BugAssist returns a non-optimal diagnosis in 2.4% (TCAS) / 9% (C-Pack-IPAs) of programs; SNIPER enumerates redundant diagnoses in 27% / 55%. C-program results; no circuit breakdown is reported.

observation_scaling.description: Paper Table 5 rows on the base tier: localisation rate for 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 failing observations (each bucket is a distinct set of 30 hidden instances).

localized_rate_obs10.description: localized_rate restricted to instances with 10 failing observations (paper Table 5 row).

localized_rate_obs20.description: localized_rate restricted to instances with 20 failing observations (paper Table 5 row).

localized_rate_obs30.description: localized_rate restricted to instances with 30 failing observations (paper Table 5 row).

localized_rate_obs40.description: localized_rate restricted to instances with 40 failing observations (paper Table 5 row).

localized_rate_obs50.description: localized_rate restricted to instances with 50 failing observations (paper Table 5 row).

localized_count_obs10.description: Audit: localized count on the 10-observation instances.

localized_count_obs20.description: Audit: localized count on the 20-observation instances.

localized_count_obs30.description: Audit: localized count on the 30-observation instances.

localized_count_obs40.description: Audit: localized count on the 40-observation instances.

localized_count_obs50.description: Audit: localized count on the 50-observation instances.

_paper_reported.note: Paper-reported numbers (augmented ISCAS85: 10 circuits, 12,147 instances, 1-50 injected faults, 10-50 observations, 1800 s per circuit on Xeon Silver 4110). Not on this gym's scale (5 circuits, 1/3/5 faults, 75 hidden instances, a few CPU-seconds per instance), so kept here for context only and never used as targets.

fault_scaling.description: Base-tier localisation rate by number of injected faults (3, 5, 7). More faults mean larger minimum diagnoses and many more of them, which is where exhaustive candidate search fails and enumeration cost dominates.

localized_rate_f7.description: localized_rate on seven-fault instances, where minimum diagnoses are largest and most numerous.

_paper_reported.note: The paper injects 1,2,3,4,5,10,20,30,40,50 faults but reports results only aggregated by observation count; no per-fault-count numbers exist.

scale_stress.description: Where the paper's method falls short: scale. The two largest ISCAS85 circuits (c5315, c7552; 2.3k-3.5k gates) with 3, 5 or 7 injected faults and 10, 30 or 50 observations (two hidden instances per cell; up to 4,000 minimum diagnoses per instance), same budget and scoring as the main experiment.

localized_rate_stress.description: localized_rate on the scale-stress tier (complete and sound minimum-diagnosis set within the per-instance CPU budget).

localized_count_stress.description: Audit: localized count on the stress tier.

budget_stop_count_stress.description: Audit: stress instances stopped by the work budget or the wall-clock guard.

_paper_reported.note: The paper's full benchmark includes these circuits (and c6288) with up to 50 faults; CFaults localises 73.84% and HSD 80.14% of all 12,147 instances within 1800 s. No per-circuit breakdown is reported.

runtime_profile.description: Paper Figure 6 (CPU-time comparison, cactus plot) on the instruction scale: share of ALL hidden instances (both tiers) localised within one half, one quarter and one eighth of the per-instance budget, read from the same run (each diagnosis is credited at the counted work at which it was observed in the output). A method that localises the same instances with less work scores higher.

localized_rate_half_budget.description: Percentage of all hidden instances localised within one half of the per-instance work budget.

localized_rate_quarter_budget.description: Percentage of all hidden instances localised within one quarter of the per-instance work budget.

localized_rate_eighth_budget.description: Percentage of all hidden instances localised within one eighth of the per-instance work budget.

localized_rate_full_budget.description: Audit: localised share of all instances (both tiers) at the full budget.

total_instances_all.description: Audit: number of hidden instances (both tiers).

_paper_reported.note: Paper Figure 6a: cactus plot of CPU time against circuits localised (no numeric table). HSD localises more circuits than CFaults at every time limit and is faster on most circuits (Figures 6b-6d).

motivating_example.description: C-program motivating example from Tables 1-2, context only.

context.scale_note: 'results' hold this gym's official hidden-test run (hardening iteration 11, final evaluator): the paper's method (cfaults) at a calibrated budget of 9.09 CPU-s per instance (speed factor 0.909), and the evaluator-owned baselines from eval/test/baseline_outputs. The paper's own numbers (10 ISCAS85 circuits, 12,147 instances, 1800 s per circuit) are not on this scale and live under each experiment's '_paper_reported'.
